stem: A patient with portal hypertension develops distal oesophageal varices. Which pair of venous pathways forms the relevant portal-to-systemic connection?

options.label: A
options.text: Superior rectal and middle rectal veins
options.explanation: These form a portosystemic connection at the rectum, not the distal oesophagus.

options.label: B
options.explanation: These form collaterals around the umbilicus rather than at the oesophageal junction.

options.label: C
options.explanation: This is a systemic-to-systemic abdominal-wall route, not the relevant portal tributary.

options.label: D
options.explanation: These connect the portal circulation to systemic veins around the distal oesophagus.

options.label: E
options.text: Hepatic veins and inferior vena cava
options.explanation: This is the normal hepatic venous outflow, not the collateral route at the distal oesophagus.

context: Left gastric tributaries communicate with oesophageal veins draining to the azygos system. Raised portal pressure can enlarge these collaterals into varices.
